subject: Emotions
title: Neural Adaptation
description: A short lesson to help you apply Neural Adaptation.

hook.text: The first bite of chocolate is heavenly. The tenth is just okay. Your neurons stopped being surprised.

buildup.text: Neural adaptation means neurons reduce their firing rate when a stimulus repeats. Novelty fades.

discovery.text: This is why you stop smelling your own home. The brain filters out the constant to focus on the new.

twist.text: Hedonic adaptation applies to life events too. Lottery winners return to baseline happiness within months.

climax.text: The brain is wired for change detection, not steady states. Surprise is the signal; calm is silence.

punchline.text: Your brain isn't built for happiness. It's built for news.

quiz.question: What is hedonic adaptation?
options: Return to baseline happiness after change
